Current focus

Optical inference of density stratification

Recovering physical structure from curved laser paths in miscible Hele-Shaw flows.

Research

Measuring what the eye cannot see directly.

Density gradients bend light. That simple fact turns an optical path into a measurement: trace the beam carefully, connect image coordinates to the experimental geometry, and fit a physical model to infer the fluid structure that produced it.

I work with Prof. Richard M. McLaughlin and collaborators on experiments in miscible stratified flow, with particular interest in overturning, interfaces, and reliable image-to-physics pipelines.

In parallel, I work with Prof. Wai-Tong (Louis) Fan on stochastic population models, comparing Wright-Fisher and multiple-merger genealogies through simulation.

02 / 04

Research project · 2026

Applied mathematics + experiments

Optical Inference of Density Stratification in Miscible Fluids via Refractive Signature Analysis

The inverse problem reduces a smooth salt-water interface to its location and thickness, represented by a low-dimensional complementary-error-function profile. A forward solver uses numerical ray shooting to predict an optical signature across controlled launch angles; regularized least squares then estimates the interface parameters from calibrated images.

I built the experimental side of this pipeline, including pixel-to-length calibration, synchronized angular scanning, trajectory extraction, and handling for strongly curved and preliminary folding paths. Repeat runs and perturbation tests provide the basis for uncertainty and repeatability checks.

  • Optical diagnostics
  • Numerical fitting
  • Computer vision
  • Uncertainty-aware calibration

Stochastic modeling

Python simulations comparing Wright-Fisher and multiple-merger ancestry models, with analysis of TMRCA, merger structure, mutations, and site- and branch-frequency spectra across replicated populations.

Experimental fluid dynamics

Obstacle-induced structure in stratified Hele-Shaw flow

Compared ideal potential flow around a circular cylinder with PIV measurements in a narrow-gap, continuously stratified Hele-Shaw cell. The ideal solution remains symmetric and vorticity-free; the experiment develops asymmetric shear layers and nonuniform structure, isolating the role of stratification, buoyancy, confinement, and viscous effects.

  • PIV/PIVlab
  • Vorticity
  • Shear layers
  • Potential flow

Instrumentation

Two-chamber injection control

A synchronized two-pump system that combines fluid streams through a mixing chamber to produce designed density profiles for tank experiments.

Beyond the lab

Statistics, mathematics, and community.

At UNC-Chapel Hill, I am completing B.S. degrees in Statistics and Analytics and Data Science, alongside a minor in Mathematics. I’m especially drawn to problems where physical intuition and computation have to agree—not just approximately, but in a way that survives contact with an actual experiment.

Outside research, I serve as President of the Badminton Club at UNC–Chapel Hill and compete in local tournaments. I was the Mixed Doubles D runner-up at the 2026 Duke Open.

Selected miscellany

Organizational archaeology and actual bird data

On LinkedIn, I describe club leadership as “organizational archaeology.” Less theatrically, I rebuilt financial and administrative workflows during a difficult leadership transition and now serve as club president.

One serious bird footnote: I combined more than 80 years of GBIF Bobolink observations with ERA5 climate data, using LOESS, regression, model comparison, and cross-validation while accounting for historical sampling bias.
